language.script: Lao script — a Brahmic-derived abugida closely related to Thai script but with simpler, more rounded letterforms and fewer consonant symbols

terrainDescription.zh: 寮國是內陸國，也是中南半島地形最多山的國家，湄公河河谷提供主要的低地農業帶，其餘地區森林覆蓋廣泛。
terrainDescription.en: Landlocked and the most mountainous country in mainland Southeast Asia, with the Mekong River valley providing the main strip of agricultural lowland and extensive forest cover elsewhere.

plate.color: black text on orange background, two-letter prefix (vehicle type/province) + serial, province name on top

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Black-and-white striped, angular (square-edged) bollards, similar in shape to Thailand's — confirm against other clues since angular bollards also appear in Sri Lanka/Philippines

utilityPole.transformerMount: Concrete poles; no further distinctive documented detail (not as sharply characterized as Thailand's full-length-pinhole poles or Cambodia's ladder poles)

historicalContext.zh: 寮語與泰語同屬壯侗語系，口語溝通大致可互通，但寮文字形較泰文簡化，筆畫較少、外觀也更圓潤、較不尖銳。
historicalContext.en: Lao and Thai are closely related Kra-Dai languages with largely mutually intelligible spoken forms, but Lao script is visually simpler — fewer letterforms and a more rounded, less angular look than Thai.
